title: The Holdovers
about: A grumpy teacher, a grieving cook and a troubled student are stuck at a New England boarding school over Christmas 1970.

    StartersMary's grilled cheese and tomato soupCreamy tomato soup with sourdough cheddar and mozzarella toastiesHow to make it1 onion, diced2 garlic cloves, crushed2 tbsp olive oil2 tins of crushed tomatoes (400g each)1 tsp smoked paprika1 tsp sugar300ml chicken stock50ml thickened cream8 slices of sourdough40g butter, soft150g vintage cheddar, grated100g mozzarella, gratedFry the onion and garlic in the oil until soft.Add the tomatoes, paprika, sugar and stock and simmer.Blitz the soup smooth and stir in the cream.Butter the outsides of the sourdough and fill with the cheddar and mozzarella.Fry over medium heat until golden on both sides. Cut into fingers and serve with the soup.Boston trip clam chowderCreamy clam chowder with bacon, potato and celeryHow to make it3 rashers of bacon, diced1 onion, diced2 celery sticks, diced2 tbsp plain flour400ml fish stock300g potatoes, diced1 small bunch thyme1kg clams, cleaned300ml thickened cream1 box oyster crackersFry the bacon until crisp, add the onion and celery and cook until soft.Stir in the flour, then the stock, potato and thyme and simmer.Add the clams, cover and cook until open, then remove the empty shells.Stir in the cream and heat through. Season with pepper and serve with oyster crackers.MainsBarton Academy Christmas roast chickenRoast chicken with sage and lemon breadcrumb stuffingHow to make it1 onion, diced80g butter150g fresh breadcrumbs1 small bunch sage, chopped1 lemon, zested1 egg1.8kg whole chicken1kg potatoes, halved3 tbsp vegetable oil4 carrots1 tbsp honey1 tbsp plain flour350ml chicken stockFry the onion in some of the butter, then mix with the breadcrumbs, sage, lemon zest and egg. Stuff the chicken.Rub the chicken with butter and salt and roast at 200°C.Roast the potatoes in oil on another tray.Glaze the carrots in butter and honey.Rest the chicken, then make gravy from the juices with the flour and stock.Mary's Christmas Eve pot roastMary cooks for the three left behindHow to make it1.5kg beef chuck roast2 tbsp vegetable oil2 brown onions3 garlic cloves2 tbsp tomato paste750ml beef stock1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce1 thyme4 carrots800g small potatoes1 tbsp cornflour1 parsleyHeat the oven to 160°C. Season the beef well and brown all over in the oil in a heavy pot. Lift out.Fry the onion wedges and garlic for 5 minutes, stir in the tomato paste, then add the stock, Worcestershire and thyme.Put the beef back, cover and braise in the oven for 2 hours.Add the carrots and halved potatoes and braise for 1 more hour until everything is tender.Lift out the beef and vegetables, thicken the juices with the cornflour mixed with a little water and simmer for 2 minutes.Slice the beef and serve with the vegetables, gravy and chopped parsley.SweetsMr Hunham's flaming cherries jubileeCherries warmed with orange and brown sugar, over vanilla ice creamHow to make it680g jar pitted cherries30g butter60g brown sugar1 orange1 tsp cornflour1 tsp vanilla extract1 L vanilla ice creamDrain the cherries, keeping some of the syrup.Melt the butter with the sugar in a wide pan, add the syrup and the orange zest and juice and simmer.Stir in the cornflour mixed with water, then add the cherries and warm through.Off the heat, stir in the vanilla and let the sauce settle for a minute.Spoon over scoops of ice cream.DrinksMr Hunham's hot honey lemon teaHot black tea, honey, lemon and cinnamon with a clove lemon sliceHow to make it4 tbsp honey3 lemons4 black tea bags800ml boiling water1/2 tsp vanilla extract4 cinnamon sticks12 clovesBoil water in a kettle.Steep a tea bag in each heatproof mug of boiling water for 3 minutes, then remove.Stir in honey, lemon juice, a drop of vanilla and a cinnamon stick until the honey dissolves.Stud a lemon slice with cloves and float it on top.
